newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mostly hold with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mostly hold with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Tuesday in lackluster trade, helped by a stable crude market and hotter East Coast weather that has stirred some demand, industry sources said.
"There's no one running out to buy, but there's no reason for sellers to panic either. The market is holding and seems balanced," said one cash trader.

Despite the heat in the Northeast, traders said forecasts for more seasonal weather later this week and next was tempering the bulls, particularly with the Southeast and Gulf Coast not expected to stray far from normal during the period.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $16.00-25 a barrel, with July one percent paper sold at $16.25 and still talked in the $16.10-25 area, up slightly on the day.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally held steady at about $16.50, but few expected much upside with only limited prospects for utility demand.
High sulphurs in New York were flat to down slightly, with 2.2 percent now talked at $14.75-15.00, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $16.00-25 and three percent at $14.50.
USG June three percent paper was pegged at $14.30-40, while August was talked at $14.50-75.

New York city gate gas prices slipped Tuesday by about a nickel to the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.31 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, fell one to two cents to $2.16/mmBtu, or $13.61 a barrel.
